transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. It's really nice to meet you. Um... I hope I'm in the right place, and I want to do whatever is helpful, so I'll just try to explain. 

I don't want to sound, you know, unreasonable or anything. But I'm here because for months now, I’ve just been trying to get people to understand what's going on with my husband’s family. They’ve been... well, they're quietly messing with our money and our good name. 

It's just these subtle things, you know? Like, I'm a billing clerk, and these little billing errors will suddenly just show up at work. Or someone at our church will just act really funny or cold toward me out of nowhere. And I know people probably think I'm making a fuss—they'll pull up all these records and try to explain it away—but I know it ties back to his family. I just know it does. 

I just really need someone to see what's happening. Does... does that make sense? Is it okay that I'm sharing this with you?
Have you ever heard or seen things that other people around you do not seem to notice?

Oh, goodness, no. Nothing like that. I... I know sometimes when people talk about being targeted, it can sound like they're imagining things, but my mind is perfectly clear. 

I've never heard voices or seen visions or anything scary like that. I just notice the real things they're doing, like the paperwork mistakes I mentioned. I promise I'm not making things up out of thin air, I just pay close attention to my surroundings. 

Does that answer your question? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information, and I definitely don't want you to think I'm... well, you know, losing touch with reality or anything.
If you were presented with concrete evidence that these billing errors and the behavior of your church members were completely unrelated to your husband's family, how would you react?

Oh... um, that's a really good question, Dr. Smith. I always try to be a reasonable person, I really do. And I know you're just trying to help me look at all the angles, which I appreciate so much. 

I guess... well, the thing is, people actually *have* tried to do that. They'll pull up all sorts of records at work to try and explain away the billing errors, or tell me that the lady at church was just having a bad day. And I listen to them, I promise I do, because I really don't want to be difficult or cause trouble for anyone. 

But... even when they show me those papers, I just... I know in my heart what's really happening. No matter what records anyone pulls up or how they try to explain it, I know it still ties back to his family. They are just so careful about it, you know? They know how to quietly mess with our money and our good name so that it *looks* like a normal mistake on paper. 

I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds so stubborn of me, and I really want to be cooperative with you. I hope you're not frustrated with me for saying that. I just have to be honest about what I know is happening... is it okay that I feel that way?
Do you feel that you have any special skills, powers, or unique insights that have made you a target for your husband's family?

Oh, my goodness, no. No, nothing like that at all. I... I really hope it's okay to say this, but I'm just a very regular person. I mean, I'm just a billing clerk, you know? I don't have any kind of special powers or... or grand insights or anything out of the ordinary. 

I'd never want to sound full of myself or make you think I'm, well, getting carried away with my imagination. I just go to work, go to church, and try to be a good wife. I think his family just... well, they just don't like me very much, and they want to cause trouble for us. That's really all it is. I'm certainly not anyone special. 

Is... is that a helpful answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need for your notes.
Have you been feeling unusually sad, hopeless, or perhaps more energetic and restless than usual during the time this has been happening?

Oh, no, doctor. I... I mean, I know it probably sounds like all of this would be terribly upsetting, but I haven't been feeling hopeless or depressed at all. I really try to keep a positive attitude, you know? And I'm definitely not... well, not restless or bouncing off the walls, either. 

I just stick to my regular routine. I go to work, I come home, I make dinner... just normal, everyday things. I don't want you to worry that I'm falling apart or acting erratic, because I promise I'm keeping myself together just fine. I'm doing my very best to handle it all calmly so I don't cause a fuss. 

Is... is that what you were asking? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture of how I'm doing, and I hope I'm being helpful.
Have you noticed similar patterns or suspicious activities involving people other than your husband's family, such as coworkers, neighbors, or strangers?

Oh... um, no. No, I haven't noticed anything like that with anyone else. 

I mean, my coworkers are all lovely people, and our neighbors are perfectly nice. I wouldn't want to accuse anyone of anything like that, especially when they've always been so kind to me. I know it must sound strange that it's just his family, and I really hope you don't think I'm just being paranoid or... or trying to find enemies everywhere I look. 

It's really just his family that seems to be doing these things. I try so hard to get along with everyone else, and I'd hate for you to think I'm the sort of person who just goes around suspecting everyone of being out to get me. I promise I'm not like that. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it clearly enough for you.
Does your husband agree with you that his family is intentionally causing these problems?

Oh... well, my husband... he doesn't really see it the way I do. I mean, he's a wonderful man, he really is, but we have had a few more arguments lately about it all. I hate fighting with him, I really do. I don't want you to think we have a bad marriage or anything, because we don't. It's just... he thinks I should just let it go. 

And, um, some of the folks at church have said similar things. There have been a few awkward moments there, just because people think I shouldn't be making a fuss about his family. I really try not to bother anyone with it, though. I'd hate for people to think I'm a difficult person. 

But I promise you, doctor, I haven't let any of this stop me from doing what I need to do. I still go to work every day, I haven't lost my job or anything terrible like that. And I still take care of the house and all my usual chores. I'm keeping up with everything, I really am. I hope that shows that I'm handling things okay, despite the disagreements. 

Is it... is it normal for husbands and wives to disagree about things like this? I just hope I'm not doing something wrong by being upset about what his family is doing.
Do you believe that these family members are working together in a coordinated, organized effort to target you, or do you feel they are acting independently?

Oh... well... I know this is going to sound just awful of me. I really hate to speak ill of anyone, especially family, and I certainly don't want to sound like I'm making up wild conspiracy stories... but, yes, I do think they are working together. 

I don't want you to think poorly of me for saying this, but for months now I’ve been trying to get people to understand that my husband’s family is quietly messing with our money and our good name. It's just... little things, but they add up. Like when little billing errors show up at my work—I notice them because of what I do—or when someone at church suddenly acts funny toward me for no reason. 

And I know people try to tell me it's just a coincidence, and no matter what records anyone pulls up to try and explain it all away, I just know it ties back to them coordinating it behind the scenes. 

I'm so sorry, I know exactly how that must sound. I really hope you don't think I'm just a vindictive or suspicious person, because I'm truly not. I'm just trying to answer your question as honestly as I can so we can figure this out. Did... did that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you ever feel like your thoughts are not your own, or that people around you can hear what you are thinking?

Oh, goodness, no. No, nothing like that at all. 

I mean, I know sometimes people can have... well, unusual experiences like that, and I don't judge anyone who does, I really don't. But my thoughts are completely my own, just normal, everyday thoughts about work and getting dinner ready and things like that. And nobody else can hear them. I'd be terribly embarrassed if anyone could hear every silly little thing that crossed my mind! 

I really just have the trouble with his family that we talked about. I don't have any of those other kinds of problems. I hope that's reassuring? I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the right answers so you don't think things are worse than they are. I'm really quite sensible most of the time, I promise.
